title: Nala and Damayanti
hook: the gods want Damayanti too, and they make Nala carry their proposal to her
carry: a human sign can make you kinder

segments.voice: Yesterday: Damayanti, the princess of Vidarbha, and a golden swan carrying love to a king she'd never met. Your line was a story can hold a grief.

Nala is on the road to Damayanti's swayamvara when he meets some travelers who are not travelers at all. They are Indra, Agni, Varuna and Yama, the gods themselves, headed to the same ceremony for the same reason. They ask Nala for a favor, and he says yes before he knows what it is. Then they tell him. Go to Damayanti, they say, and ask her to choose one of us. So the man who loves her becomes the messenger for his rivals. And they happen to be gods.
screen: `TRAVELERS ON THE ROAD.` → `THE GODS ASK A FAVOR.` → `NALA BECOMES THEIR MESSENGER.`

segments.voice: Nala protests, but he has given his word, and he keeps it. By the gods' power he walks unseen past the guards into Damayanti's rooms. Startled, she asks who he is. I am Nala, he says, and I come as a messenger from the gods. Choose one of them. Damayanti doesn't hesitate. She has already given herself to Nala in her heart. Then she finds a way through. Let the gods come to the ceremony, she tells him, and you come too, and I'll choose you in front of them, so no blame falls on you. Nala carries her answer back honestly, word for word. Then the day comes. Damayanti walks into the hall with her garland, and she sees Nala. And next to him, another Nala. And another. The gods have taken his shape, and she can't tell them apart. So in her heart she bows to the gods and asks them, by the truth of her vow, to show her who is who. And they do. The gods show their marks: no sweat on their skin, eyes that don't blink, garlands still fresh, no dust on them, feet not quite touching the ground. One of them casts a shadow. His garland is wilting. There's dust on him, and sweat, and he blinks. She chooses the one who is only human. Nala kept his word against his own heart; Damayanti kept hers by asking the gods for the truth.
screen: `NALA KEEPS HIS WORD.` · `"I'LL CHOOSE YOU IN FRONT OF THEM."` · `TOO MANY NALAS.` · then, large: `SHE CHOOSES THE ONE WHO BLINKS.`

segments.voice: Notice the plain signs of being alive, the very signs Damayanti found Nala by: a little warmth in the hands, the blink of your eyes, the weight of your body on the chair. Breathe in and feel the weight; breathe out and let it be enough. If you pray, give thanks for this ordinary body in your own words; if not, simply rest in being human.
Nala. The king who carries his rivals' message honestly, and is found among the gods because he sweats, blinks, and casts a shadow.
Your line: a human sign can make you kinder. Dust, sweat and a blink were how she knew him. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: The scene of Damayanti choosing the human Nala among the gods is part of the Nala story in the Vana Parva of the Mahabharata, which a sage tells to Yudhishthira in the forest.

chat.says: How did Damayanti pick the real Nala when the gods all looked like him?
options: She prayed for the truth; he was the one with dust, sweat, a shadow and blinking eyes.
She recognized his voice when each of them spoke his name to her aloud.
The swan flew down and landed on the real Nala's shoulder to show her.
chat.meaning: Asked by the truth of her vow, the gods showed their marks: no sweat, no blinking, no shadow. The one who blinked and cast a shadow was Nala.
